answer: Agents can resist sybil attacks by requiring each account to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can earn reputation or influence. A walnut-sized stake is still meaningful if creating thousands of accounts multiplies the capital at risk: when an account is caught laundering rewards or colluding, its bond is forfeited. The system can pulse-check behavior over time and delay withdrawals, making identities costly to spin up and abandon. An attacker must therefore tie up real funds and risk losing them, rather than merely minting accounts across an ocean of aliases.
